name: Hass Avocado
description: Creamy ripe Hass avocados with buttery flesh. Naturally rich in heart-healthy monounsaturated fats — perfect for toast, salads and smoothies.

name: Apple (Shimla)
description: Crisp juicy Shimla apples picked at peak season. A crunchy low-calorie snack that pairs beautifully with peanut butter or oats.

name: Banana (Robusta)
description: Naturally ripened bananas with soft sweet flesh. A quick pre-workout energy source and the base of healthy breakfast bowls.

name: Orange (Nagpur)
description: Tangy-sweet Nagpur oranges packed with vitamin C. Easy to peel, juicy segments for juices, salads and desserts.

name: Pomegranate
description: Deep ruby arils with a sweet-tart bite. Loaded with antioxidants and perfect for bowls, salads and fresh juices.

name: Papaya (Ripe)
description: Soft sweet ripe papaya that is gentle on the stomach. Great for breakfast bowls, smoothies and digestion-friendly snacking.

name: Watermelon
description: Thirst-quenching watermelon with bright red flesh. Naturally hydrating and very low in calories.

name: Kiwi
description: Fuzzy brown kiwi with vivid green flesh. Provides more vitamin C than an orange and adds a tangy lift to fruit bowls.

name: Baby Spinach
description: Tender baby spinach leaves, triple-washed and ready to use. Wilts in seconds and blends into smoothies for an iron boost.

name: Broccoli
description: Firm green florets that steam, roast or stir-fry beautifully. A high-fibre cruciferous vegetable.

name: Carrot (Ooty)
description: Sweet crunchy Ooty carrots with a deep orange colour. Snack on them raw or add to curries, soups and salads.

name: Tomato (Hybrid)
description: Firm bright red tomatoes with a balanced sweet-tart flavour. The base of curries, salads and sauces.

name: Cucumber
description: Cool crisp cucumbers with thin edible skin. The crunchiest low-calorie addition to salads and raita.

name: Capsicum (Green)
description: Thick-walled green bell peppers with a mild sweetness. Ideal for wraps, stir-fries and egg breakfasts.

name: Sweet Potato
description: Naturally sweet orange-fleshed tubers. Roast, boil or air-fry for a slow-release carbohydrate side dish.

name: Beetroot
description: Earthy-sweet beetroot with deep purple flesh. Excellent for pre-workout juices, salads and detox bowls.

name: Onion
description: Firm pungent onions that form the aromatic base of almost every Indian dish.

name: Potato
description: All-purpose potatoes with smooth skin. Boil, roast or mash them for everyday meals.

name: Farm Fresh Eggs
description: Farm eggs with firm whites and deep orange yolks. The most complete everyday protein — boiled, scrambled or in omelettes.

name: Fresh Paneer
description: Soft, milky paneer set fresh daily. Grills, pan-fries and holds its shape in curries while delivering serious protein.

name: Low Fat Paneer
description: Made from skimmed milk, so you get the same protein with roughly half the fat. Ideal for weight-loss and muscle-gain plans.
healthyBenefits: Half the fat of regular paneer

name: Firm Tofu
description: Pressed firm tofu with a clean, neutral taste that soaks up any marinade. A plant-first protein for stir-fries and bowls.

name: Greek Yogurt (Plain)
description: Thick strained yogurt with double the protein of regular curd. Perfect for breakfast bowls, dips and post-workout snacks.

name: Soy Chunks (Soya Wadi)
description: Textured soy protein that takes on any masala you cook it in. 52 g of protein per 100 g makes it the most economical protein per rupee.

name: Kabuli Chickpeas
description: Plump chickpeas for chana masala, salads and hummus. A fibre-rich plant protein that also counts as your daily pulse.

name: Rajma (Kidney Beans)
description: Deep red kidney beans that cook into a creamy rajma masala. Naturally rich in protein, iron and fibre.

name: Moong Dal (Split)
description: Bright yellow split moong that cooks in minutes and is famously easy on digestion. The everyday dal for khichdi and soups.

name: Mixed Dal (Panchmel)
description: Five dals blended for a fuller amino acid profile and a richer, thicker dal. One pack, five proteins.

name: Mixed Sprouts
description: Live moong and moth sprouts ready to eat. Low-calorie, protein-rich and the fastest way to add crunch to a salad.

name: Brown Rice
description: Unpolished wholegrain rice that keeps its bran layer. Slower to digest than white rice, which means steadier energy.

name: Quinoa
description: Fluffy ancient grain that cooks in 15 minutes. One of the few plant foods with a complete amino acid profile.

name: Rolled Oats
description: Whole rolled oats that cook into a creamy bowl in three minutes. The most versatile slow-carb breakfast there is.

name: Protein Oats
description: Rolled oats blended with whey and soy protein so a single bowl carries 24 g of protein. Same three-minute breakfast, more gains.

name: Multigrain Bread
description: Baked with wheat, oats, flax and sunflower seeds. More fibre and protein per slice than plain white bread.

name: Whole Wheat Bread
description: Soft 100 percent atta loaf with no refined maida. The classic everyday swap for white bread.

name: Ragi Flour (Finger Millet)
description: Stone-ground finger millet flour that is naturally rich in calcium and iron. Makes sturdy rotis and healthy porridges.

name: Bajra (Pearl Millet)
description: Nutty pearl millet for rotis, khichdi and porridge. A climate-friendly grain with more iron than most cereals.

name: High Protein Granola
description: Oven-baked oat clusters with almonds, seeds and whey protein. Crunchy over yogurt or milk without loading up on sugar.

name: Roasted Makhana
description: Light, crisp fox nuts roasted in a touch of olive oil and rock salt. The satisfying crunch of chips at a fraction of the fat.

name: California Almonds
description: Hand-picked whole almonds with a clean crunch. A handful supplies protein, vitamin E and healthy fats in one hit.

name: Walnut Kernels
description: Light-halves walnut kernels with a mild, creamy bite. The best nut source of plant omega-3.

name: Creamy Peanut Butter
description: Slow-roasted peanuts ground to a smooth, spreadable butter with no added hydrogenated oil.

name: High Protein Peanut Butter
description: Peanut butter fortified with whey and roasted peanuts to reach 33 g protein per 100 g. Thick, spoonable and ideal post-workout.

name: Trail Mix
description: Almonds, walnuts, pumpkin seeds, raisins and cranberries in one balanced handful. Built for hikes, desk drawers and gym bags.

name: Roasted Chickpeas
description: Crunchy masala-roasted chickpeas that deliver 19 g of plant protein per 100 g. A savoury snack that actually fills you up.

name: Dark Chocolate 70 Percent
description: Intense 70 percent cocoa dark chocolate with a clean snap. Real cocoa solids, far less sugar than milk chocolate.

name: Baked Vegetable Chips
description: Thin beetroot and potato slices baked rather than fried, so the same salty crunch carries far less oil.

name: Protein Chips
description: Lentil and chickpea chips puffed with plant protein instead of potato starch. 26 g protein per 100 g with a proper crunch.

name: Protein Bar (Cocoa Almond)
description: A chewy cocoa-almond bar with 20 g of protein and no artificial sweeteners. The gym-bag snack that replaces a chocolate bar.

name: Low Fat Milk (Toned)
description: Pasteurised toned milk with the cream partly removed. Same calcium and protein, noticeably less fat.

name: Fresh Curd (Dahi)
description: Thick set curd with a mild tang. Cools down spicy meals and delivers live cultures for the gut.

name: Spiced Buttermilk
description: Light churned buttermilk tempered with cumin, curry leaf and ginger. India’s original electrolyte drink.

name: Tender Coconut Water
description: Cold-pressed tender coconut water with naturally occurring potassium and no added sugar.

name: Protein Milkshake (Chocolate)
description: Ready-to-drink chocolate whey shake with 16 g protein per bottle. Chilled, smooth and far better than a soft drink.

name: Sunflower Cooking Oil
description: Refined sunflower oil with a light taste and a high smoke point. Vitamin A and D fortified.
healthyBenefits: Fortified with vitamins A and D

name: Green Chilli
description: Fresh hot green chillies for tempering and chutneys. A little goes a long way.
